entries.detail: Ran grep -niE for chart|pie|graph|axis|plot|bar|donut|gauge|3d across all five target files (QuestionnaireDetailView.swift, QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift, QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift, REDESIGN_SPECS.md, DerivedImportance.swift). No chart, graph, dashboard, or data-visualization code or spec exists in any target: the Swift files are questionnaire UI/viewmodel/browse flows with no chart marks, and the two REDESIGN_SPECS.md hits ('iconography', 'named for what it was copied from') are unrelated prose, not chart references. This rule (chart type must follow the question, not the data shape) addresses a data-visualization artifact that is absent from these targets.
entries.rule_title: Chart type follows the question, not the data shape

entries.detail: Rule targets categorical chart/dashboard colors. Ran grep -inE "chart|graph|plot|dashboard|barChart|LineChart|PieChart|Color(" across all five targets (QuestionnaireDetailView.swift, QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift, QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift, REDESIGN_SPECS.md, DerivedImportance.swift). The only Color(...) hits are `.foregroundColor(DesignTokens.Colors.inkMuted/ink)` calls on plain Text labels (QuestionnaireDetailView.swift lines 39,47,110,128,132,145; QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift lines 26,61,67) — these are UI text tinting, not chart series colors. DerivedImportance.swift is a matching-score computation with no visualization code. REDESIGN_SPECS.md's only "chart/graph/plot"-adjacent hits (lines 167, 403) are the word "iconography" substring matches, not chart content. No chart, graph, plot, or dashboard rendering exists in any of these five targets, so there is no categorical palette to audit.
entries.rule_title: Categorical colors come from a validated palette and survive both themes

entries.detail: Ran `grep -n -i "gradient|Color(hue|LinearGradient|scale|heatmap|chart|diverging|sequential"` across all three Swift targets and REDESIGN_SPECS.md, and separately grepped DerivedImportance.swift for "gradient|Color|scale|heatmap|chart". None of the targets contain a color-encoded chart, heatmap, or data-magnitude palette. QuestionnaireDetailView.swift/QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift only use DesignTokens.Colors.ink/inkMuted/surface (static semantic text/background tokens, not scales) and REDESIGN_SPECS.md's "gradient" mentions (lines 11-427) all concern chrome/hero decoration explicitly, which the spec forbids using as data encoding ("no gradient-as-chrome"). The one numeric visualization referenced, the "importance track's cumulative fill" (REDESIGN_SPECS.md line 768), is described as a monochrome fill bar, not a hue ramp, and DerivedImportance.swift (Sources/App/Matching/DerivedImportance.swift) computes only a numeric shrinkage score with no color output. DV-003 addresses sequential/diverging color scales on charts and dashboards; no such chart exists in this target set, so the rule does not apply.
entries.rule_title: Sequential and diverging scales are used for their own data shapes

entries.detail: Rule DV-004 addresses axes, legends, and tooltips on data visualizations (charts and dashboards). The target files contain only UI layouts, list views, view models, and server-side calculations. No charts, graphs, plots, or data visualizations are present in any of the five targets.
entries.rule_title: Axes, legends, and tooltips are complete and honest

entries.detail: akin/Flows/Social/QuestionnaireDetailView.swift:46 - `Text(count.value).font(.headline)` -> use `.font(.caption)` for the numeral to match REDESIGN_SPECS.md:744-745 ("a single row of three counts at `type-scale.caption`") and to match the numeral treatment used for the same derived-importance metric elsewhere in the same flow: QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift's importance chip renders its numeral at `.font(.caption)` (grep confirmed: `Text(QuestionnaireBrowseViewModel.importanceText(for: row)).font(.caption)` in the BrowseRow of QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift). The Detail screen's three-count row (Respondents/Completed/Importance) instead renders its numeral at `.font(.headline)`, a visibly larger and different numeral treatment for the identical "Importance" figure shown between the two screens in the same feature, and a direct deviation from the spec's own stated type scale for that row. Everything else checked was consistent: both view models format percentages identically (`String(format: "%.0f%%", score * 100)` in QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift:61 and QuestionnaireBrowseViewModel.swift:56), and both use the identical empty-state string "Not rated yet" for the unrated case, so this is a real, isolated numeral-treatment inconsistency, not a systemic one. DerivedImportance.swift (akin-server-side) is backend calculation code with no UI rendering, so it is not applicable to this rule. I did not run or render the app (no build/UI rendering was permitted or attempted); this finding is based on static reading of the SwiftUI view code and the design spec, not a rendered side-by-side comparison, which is a limitation of my coverage relative to the rule's stated detection method.
entries.rule_title: Stat tiles, meters, and sparklines follow one system

entries.detail: Rule DV-006 targets charts/dashboards where an unmeasured value could be plotted as a zero indistinguishable from a real zero. I grep'd all five targets (QuestionnaireDetailView.swift, QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift, QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift, REDESIGN_SPECS.md, DerivedImportance.swift) for chart/plot/graph/Chart/BarMark/LineMark/PointMark/Sparkline/dashboard/import Charts and found zero matches. QuestionnaireDetailView/ViewModel/BrowseView (164, 77, 90 lines) are SwiftUI questionnaire browsing/detail UI with no data-viz rendering; REDESIGN_SPECS.md (935 lines) is a design spec doc whose only near-hit was 'romance iconography' text, not chart terminology; DerivedImportance.swift (121 lines) computes an importance score server-side but does not plot or render it anywhere in this file. None of these targets contain a chart, graph, or dashboard artifact for this rule to apply to.
entries.rule_title: Numbers in a chart are the real measurement
